chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman said:

I wrote to the Faqih (peace be upon him) asking him about the Qunut, so he wrote to me: 'If there is a severe necessity, do not raise the two hands, and say three times: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful."'.

key_terms.بِسْمِ اَللّهِ اَلرَّحْمنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

ai.seo_question: What is the correct method for performing Qunut during severe necessity according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Faqih (often identified as Imam al-Hadi or Imam al-Hasan in the context of Qunut rulings) clarifies the specific manner of performing Qunut during times of severe distress (darurah). Unlike the general practice of raising hands, this ruling prescribes keeping the hands still and reciting 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim' three times, highlighting the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding supplicatory acts during prayer based on the intensity of the need.
